title: One codebase, many versions: build the newest response, then undo each change back to the client's version
captions: An old client calls the API. Its account was pinned to version 2024-01-15 on its first request, so every call is served in that version.
The API code only knows one shape: the newest. It builds the response the way a client on 2025-03-01 would see it.
A translation layer walks back in time. The 2025-03-01 change turned one email into a list, so this step turns the list back into one email.
The 2024-06-01 change replaced the verified true/false field with a status text. This step turns the status back into true or false.
The old client gets exactly the shape it was written for. A newer client skips the steps it does not need. Each old rule lives in one place.
